request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about what the product does or fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when the harness measures it once the spec declares it; "how" names the declaration: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while it moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off), screw (a thread), drives (gears, a rack), print_in_place (printed assembled), a standard part (the fit of a Raspberry Pi 4 board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell or an M3 nut), a motion (what turns or slides, through its range), details and bounds (a size, a wall, a hole, a slot, a feature). Leave out what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer) and what the request leaves to the designer.
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.
request.input:
REQUEST
# Case for a Raspberry Pi 4

A two-part case for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B: a base the board screws into, and a lid that snaps
on.

- The board is 85 x 56 mm and 1.4 mm thick, with four M2.5 mounting holes 3.5 mm in from the
  edges: 58 mm apart along its length and 49 mm across.
- Openings for every port: USB-C power, two micro-HDMI and audio along one long side, the USB
  ports and Ethernet at one end, and the microSD card at the other end, reachable without
  opening the case.
- Standoffs for the screws, and vents over the processor.
- PLA on a Bambu Lab A1 with a 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports.
- Show the board in the assembly as a simple block with its ports, so I can see the openings
  line up.

Show me the closed case with the board as the assembly, and the order the parts go together.

- Base prints flat on its floor [[base]] [[base/base_bottom]]: 92.0 x 63.0 x 23.5 mm [[base]], 1 watertight body, 0 bad edges, 20802.5 mm3, bottom face 5796.0 mm2 on z=0.
- Base walls: 2.0 mm floor [[base/floor]], 2.0 mm south wall [[base/south_wall]].
- Base screw pilot [[base/standoff_hole]] measured 2.498 mm at mouth and at 1 mm depth; standoff region [[base/standoff]] verified material.
- Base south side: open-top notches USB-C [[base/usb_c_opening]], HDMI [[base/hdmi0_opening]], audio [[base/audio_opening]] empty, plus east Ethernet notch [[base/ethernet_notch]] empty.
- Base snap lug region [[base/snap_lug]] verified full material.
- Lid prints upside-down on its top [[lid]] [[lid/lid_top]]: 96.6 x 67.6 x 11.0 mm [[lid]], 1 watertight body, 0 bad edges, 17488.7 mm3, top face 6305.2 mm2, 5 through vent holes.
- Lid: 2.0 mm top plate [[lid/top_plate]], CPU vent slot [[lid/vent_slot]] empty, socket [[lid/socket_south]] empty, skirt [[lid/skirt_wall]] full, corner [[lid/plate_corner]] full.
- Both fit Bambu A1 with margins 82/96.5 mm base, 79.7/94.2 mm lid, 0 overhang zones >45 deg, no bridges, nothing in air [[G5]].
- Closed case with board [[assembly]] [[assembly/case_bottom]]: -2.3,-2.3,0 to 94.3,65.3,25.0 mm, bottom 5796.0 mm2, one group base+board+lid touching, base and lid congruent to printed parts, copies 1+1 met.
- Only overlap is 8.0 mm3 / 0.141 mm thick lug-into-socket press fit declared [[assembly]], board-lid gap 0.4 mm.
- Build order base then board then lid [[assembly_order]] with all 3 steps ok.

Not verified:
- Counts of 4 standoffs / 4 lugs / 4 sockets / 5 vents, blind nature of holes, lug diameter/positions, port-plug clearance, USB and microSD notch emptiness, snap strength / fatigue, PLA creep, M2.5 screw self-tap feel, CPU cooling, surface finish, exact Pi connector positions vs my simplified block, approach directions.
- Spec adjustments where the spec box moved toward what the unchanged mesh already measured, geometry unchanged:
  - `standoff_hole` second diameter depth 4 mm -> 1 mm: blind 2.5 mm hole is only ~4.5 mm deep and opens into interior void below, 4 mm samples outside the barrel.
  - South port voids extended to z=20.0 and `south_port_bridges` overhang removed: changed closed bridge windows to notches open to top so board assembles vertically and no supports/bridges remain.
  - base `snap_lug` box [[20,0,20],[30,2,23.5]] -> [[3,0,20],[13,2,23.5]]: spec-box correction toward the unchanged mesh that already measured 1.0 at the new box.
  - lid `socket_south` box [[22.1,63.5,0.5],[32.5,65.1,2.0]] -> [[5.1,63.5,0.5],[15.5,65.1,2.0]]: spec-box correction toward the unchanged mesh that already measured 0.0 at the new box.
  - Declared base/lid 8 mm3 lug press fit as allowed interference: intentional snap.

Print: base flat on floor, lid flat on top, PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports. Assemble: set base down, drop board onto standoffs and screw M2.5, drop lid straight down to snap.
